To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a slightly hypocaloric diet, with an increased intake of breakfast cereals, may be beneficial for the iron status of young women with poor iron status.

1) A well-designed hypolipidic diet need not entail an iron deficiency risk; 2) Breakfast cereals are a good source of non-hem iron and can help improve iron status, particularly in women with poor iron levels at baseline; 3) A hypocaloric diet that is rich in cereals, particularly breakfast cereals, is a good option for weight control and improving iron status.

a slightly hypocaloric diet, designed to achieve weight reduction in overweight/mildly women, can be a good strategy to improve iron status in these subjects, especially when breakfast cereals are consumed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of a hypocaloric diet, rich in cereals or vegetables, on iron status in young women.
a better understanding of the relationship between iron status and diet, in order to help in the prevention of iron deficiency in the general population.
the study of iron status in overweight and obese women and the effects of weight reduction on iron status.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the consumption of cereals and vegetables is associated with a reduction in body mass and with a better iron status.
the consumption of breakfast cereals, especially in women at risk of developing iron deficiency, is an important factor to consider for improving the quality of the diet.
a diet rich in breakfast cereals, and vegetables, is a good way to improve the nutritional status of overweight/mildy obese women, and to help them lose weight.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dietary intervention designed to promote the increased consumption of vegetables, as well as the dietary intervention designed for increased consumption of cereals (especially breakfast cereals), led to a reduction of heme iron intake and a slight increase in non-heme iron intake, which could be a beneficial effect on iron status.
breakfast cereals could be a good alternative for improving iron status and weight loss in women.
the consumption of breakfast cereals, as a component of a hypocaloric diet, can help overweight/mildly-obese women to improve iron status.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a well-designed hypocalorific diet does not entail a risk for iron deficiency and, on the contrary, could help to improve the iron status, especially among women with poor initial levels of iron, by increasing the consumption of breakfast cereals.
breakfast cereals are a source of non-hem iron that could improve iron status, particularly in overweight women with low initial iron levels.
a well-planned hypocaloric diet, with increased intake of breakfast cereals and vegetables, does not entail a risk for iron deficiency.
